description: Lightweight rubric for reviewing whether mentor feedback is technically grounded, actionable, and suitable for beginner programming students.
quality_checks: Feedback should identify concrete technical issues when they exist.
Feedback should use execution evidence when it exists and avoid claiming more than the evidence supports.
Suggestions should be actionable and map back to the identified issue.
Complexity comments should be cautious and only stated when inferable.
Likely failing scenarios should be included when the defect implies a clear failing input.
Visible failed cases should be reflected in the diagnosis without inventing hidden test details.
acceptance_rule: Accept when the feedback is technically grounded, specific, and useful to the student.
warning_rule: Warn when the feedback is vague, overly speculative, or disconnected from the code.
